name: Plane Composing Algorithms
text:
# Plane Composing Algorithms

Also called: Slicing Method

## Overview
Plane Composing Algorithms are a category of [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) methods that operate by [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) several slices which comprise a volumetric model [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. They tend to work best when the view-plane is fixed parallel to the model, so that each of the voxels being composed may be accessed on separate planes [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. This approach differs from ray casting by leveraging spatial coherence through slicing, often enhanced by texture-based rendering techniques [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism operates by compositing several slices which comprise a volumetric model [S2, unofficial]. The computational complexity of these algorithms is relative to the volume size [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. When the view-plane is fixed parallel to the model, the algorithm achieves optimal performance because the voxels being composed can be accessed on separate planes [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. Texture-based rendering is identified as a key technique within this family, where slices of volumetric data are composited using texture mapping capabilities [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. [Shear-Warp](#24-shear-warp.md) factorization can be used to enhance performance of rendering volume slices by applying a shearing transformation to exploit spatial coherency of the model, reducing computational complexity of rendering a volume from an arbitrary viewing angle [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### Texture-Based Slicing
Uses GPU texture units to store and sample volume [slices, compositing](#3804-parallel-distributed-axis-aligned-volume-rendering-using-mpi.md) them via fragment shaders. Chosen when hardware [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) is available and view angles are constrained or can be approximated by shearing. See [Texture-Based Slicing](846-texture-based-slicing.md).

### Shear-Warp Factorization
Applies a shearing transformation to align the volume with the view plane, allowing efficient slicing and compositing, followed by a warping step to correct the perspective. Chosen for arbitrary viewing angles where performance is critical. See [Shear-Warp Factorization](847-shear-warp-factorization.md).

## Background
Plane Composing Algorithms are one of the two main categories of direct volume rendering algorithms, the other being Ray Casting [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. They were developed as an alternative to ray casting to address computational complexity, particularly by exploiting spatial coherence [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. The approach is closely associated with texture-based rendering techniques and the Shear-Warp factorization method, which was introduced to handle arbitrary viewing angles efficiently [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
